description: Let the selected service reuse recent cacheable responses instead of asking downstream systems every time.
useful_when: Use when repeated reads are pushing unnecessary work into the database path.
expected_benefits: Improves read latency and reduces persistence pressure when requests repeat.
tradeoffs: Cache behavior can hide downstream pressure and stale entries may require explicit clearing.
pressure_shifts: Persistence pressure can shift into cache memory pressure

description: Limit incoming traffic so the system can drain queues instead of accepting more work than it can process.
useful_when: Use when overload is spreading faster than capacity can be added.
expected_benefits: Protects core systems and reduces cascading failure risk.
tradeoffs: Sacrifices some throughput or user access to preserve stability.
pressure_shifts: Traffic pressure shifts toward user-facing latency

description: Increase local processing capacity for the selected API service.
useful_when: Use when API utilization and API queue pressure are the dominant bottleneck.
expected_benefits: Raises request processing throughput at the selected service.
tradeoffs: Does not fix downstream database, cache, or network bottlenecks.
negative_effects: Downstream database pressure can become more visible
pressure_shifts: Compute relief can shift bottlenecks toward persistence

description: Add a cache into the selected dependency path so repeated reads can be absorbed before reaching storage.
useful_when: Use when database pressure comes from repeated read-heavy traffic.
expected_benefits: Moves repeated read work away from persistence and can improve regional latency.
tradeoffs: Adds topology complexity and may require cache placement decisions.
negative_effects: Memory usage and invalidation complexity increase
pressure_shifts: Persistence pressure can shift into cache state management

description: Add read capacity near a chosen region to reduce pressure on the primary database.
useful_when: Use when read-heavy traffic saturates persistence but writes are not the main issue.
expected_benefits: Improves read throughput and reduces primary database pressure.
tradeoffs: Adds replication complexity and may introduce stale reads.
positive_effects: Read pressure spreads across persistence nodes
negative_effects: Replication overhead and stale-read risk increase
pressure_shifts: Write/replication pressure can become the next bottleneck

description: Insert a queue into a dependency path so bursts become backlog that downstream workers or storage can drain over time.
useful_when: Use when short spikes create instability but downstream work can be smoothed over time.
expected_benefits: Absorbs bursts and turns immediate overload into a backlog that can drain.
tradeoffs: Improves stability but can increase waiting time if workers cannot catch up.
negative_effects: End-to-end latency and consistency complexity increase
Delayed work becomes a backlog that workers must drain
pressure_shifts: Queue pressure moves from database saturation into buffering

description: Place cache capacity near regional demand to reduce repeated long-distance reads.
useful_when: Use when distant users repeatedly request the same data.
expected_benefits: Cuts cross-region read latency and reduces load on the origin region.
tradeoffs: Adds regional consistency and invalidation complexity.
positive_effects: Regional traffic stays closer to users
negative_effects: Distributed state and cache coordination increase
pressure_shifts: Central persistence pressure shifts toward regional cache operations

description: Enable or disable retries to trade user-visible failures against retry amplification.
useful_when: Use when timeouts either need temporary recovery attempts or retries are making overload worse.
expected_benefits: Can improve recovery from transient failures or stop retry storms.
tradeoffs: Retries can protect users from brief failures, but they can also multiply load during incidents.
positive_effects: Overloaded services receive less repeated work
negative_effects: Disabling retries can expose more user-visible failures
pressure_shifts: Reliability pressure shifts between retries and visible errors

description: Evict current cache contents when cached behavior is masking or amplifying a problem.
useful_when: Use when stale or misleading cached data makes pressure hard to interpret.
expected_benefits: Resets cache state and makes fresh downstream behavior visible.
tradeoffs: Temporarily increases database load while the cache warms again.
positive_effects: Reveals cache dependency and recovery behavior
negative_effects: Database pressure and latency may spike while cache warms
pressure_shifts: Read pressure shifts from cache back to persistence

description: Clear cached responses to free memory and force fresh downstream reads.
useful_when: Use only when stale or poisoned cached data is the real problem, not when read traffic is already stressing storage.
expected_benefits: Can remove stale entries and temporarily reduce cache memory pressure.
tradeoffs: Often worsens latency and database pressure by forcing a cache miss storm.
pressure_shifts: Cache pressure shifts into persistence pressure

description: Add API processing power even when the visible symptoms may be caused by a downstream database bottleneck.
useful_when: Use when API compute is truly the root bottleneck. It is a trap when queues are caused by downstream persistence.
expected_benefits: May reduce local API queueing if compute is saturated.
tradeoffs: Can push more requests into an already overloaded database path.
negative_effects: Extra capacity may solve the wrong layer
pressure_shifts: Compute pressure shifts into persistence pressure
